enriched_description: Circular or rectangular flush iron cover set into a street or sidewalk surface. The cover has a heavy cast iron construction with a rough textured surface featuring a raised pattern of concentric circles, diamond grid, or parallel ridges for traction. Diameter ranges from 45-65 cm for circular covers. The surface includes raised lettering indicating the utility type (water, sewer, electric). Two small holes near the edge serve as lift points for a hook tool. The cover sits flush with the surrounding pavement, with a narrow gap visible around the perimeter. Color is dark gray or black from weathered iron.

Percussion instrument consisting of a hollow oval-shaped gourd or synthetic shell mounted on a cylindrical handle. The shell is approximately 8-15 cm long and contains loose pebbles, seeds, or beads that rattle when shaken. Surface of the shell may be natural dried gourd with a matte textured finish, painted in bright colors, or wrapped in woven material. The handle extends 10-20 cm from the shell, made of wood or plastic with a smooth grip. Often used in pairs, one in each hand. The shell has a smooth rounded profile tapering to the handle attachment point.

Percussion instrument consisting of a series of wooden bars arranged in a keyboard layout similar to a piano, mounted over tubular metal resonators. The bars are made of rosewood or synthetic material with a smooth polished surface, arranged in two rows (naturals and accidentals) spanning 4-5 octaves. Each bar is approximately 3-5 cm wide and varies in length from 10 cm (highest notes) to 50+ cm (lowest notes). Beneath each bar hangs a vertical aluminum resonator tube. The frame is constructed of metal tubing with adjustable height legs. Played with yarn-wrapped mallets held in each hand.

Face covering designed to disguise or conceal the wearer's identity, shaped to fit over the facial features. Construction varies from rigid molded plastic or papier-mache to flexible fabric or leather. The mask has cutout openings for the eyes and sometimes the mouth and nose. Surface features painted or sculpted details representing faces, animals, or abstract designs. Full-face masks cover from forehead to chin, while half-masks cover the upper face. Attachment is via elastic straps, ribbon ties, or a handle. Surface texture ranges from smooth painted finish to textured fabric weave.

Short thin wooden stick approximately 4-5 cm long and 2 mm square in cross-section, with a colored chemical head at one end. The wooden shaft has a light tan color with visible wood grain texture. The head is a rounded or slightly flattened bulb approximately 4-6 mm in diameter, colored red, brown, or blue depending on the match type. The head surface has a slightly rough granular texture from the combustible chemical coating. The opposite end of the stick is plain cut wood. Multiple matchsticks are typically stored in a matchbox with a striking surface.

Tall vertical wooden pole standing 5-15 meters high, decorated with colorful ribbons or streamers attached at the top. The pole is cylindrical with a smooth painted surface, typically white or natural wood color. Streamers in multiple bright colors (red, blue, yellow, green, pink) extend from the top to the ground, each approximately 2-3 meters long. The pole is mounted in a fixed base, often surrounded by a circular platform or grassy area. Dancers hold individual streamers and weave around the pole in patterns. The top may feature a decorative finial, wreath, or flag.

Complex network of interconnected paths and dead ends designed as a puzzle to navigate from entrance to exit. Garden mazes feature tall hedges (1-3 meters high) forming walls with a narrow walking path between them. Hedge surfaces are dense green foliage with a textured leafy appearance. Indoor or corn mazes use wooden walls, cornstalks, or printed panels. The layout viewed from above shows an intricate geometric pattern with branching paths, cul-de-sacs, and a central goal area. Path width is typically 1-1.5 meters, sufficient for single-file or two-person passage.

Transparent or translucent graduated container used for measuring liquid or dry ingredients in cooking. Typically made of glass or clear plastic with a cylindrical or slightly tapered body. Volume markings are printed or etched on the side in milliliters, cups, and ounces with horizontal lines and numerical labels. Capacity ranges from 250 ml (1 cup) to 1 liter (4 cups). A pouring spout extends from the rim on one side. A handle is attached to the side opposite the spout. The base is flat and stable. Liquid level is read against the graduated markings at eye level.

Wall-mounted or freestanding cabinet designed to store medicines and toiletries, typically installed in a bathroom. The cabinet has a rectangular box shape with a hinged door, often featuring a mirror on the exterior face. Dimensions approximately 30-60 cm wide by 40-80 cm tall by 10-20 cm deep. Interior contains one or more adjustable shelves creating compartments for organizing bottles, tubes, and containers. Construction is wood, metal, or plastic with a white, wood-grain, or mirrored finish. The mirror door reflects the room when closed. Mounting brackets are visible on the rear panel.

Massive prehistoric stone structure consisting of one or more very large upright stones, often arranged in a circular or linear pattern. Individual stones are rough-hewn natural rock with an irregular surface texture showing weathering, lichen growth, and erosion patterns. Stones range from 2-10 meters in height with a width of 1-3 meters. The stone surface is gray, brown, or greenish from mineral content and biological growth. Some megaliths are arranged as trilithons (two vertical stones supporting a horizontal lintel). The base of each stone is partially buried in the ground, surrounded by grass or earth.
